correctness.rationale: For each r the signature at round r decodes the isometry type of the radius-delta_r class by induction, since the counts of prior colours in radius-delta_(r+1) decode the populations of lower-radius ball types and division by each ball cardinality gives their multiplicities. At r=h-1 the global histogram reconstructs the final top-level partition. At h=3 the 1-round signature of x encodes (size of delta1 ball, size of delta2 ball,n). All subpartitions of q<=3 are uniquely decodable, and n<=7 has no duplicate large q>=4 balls. At n=8 the sole possible collision is two q=4 balls, with the unique integer trade 2*(2,1,1) versus (2,2)+(1,1,1,1). Script enumerate all 223 eight-point types and verifies one pair, with no two-round collisions through 8. The proof is unbounded; script is a finite check only.

value.rationale: Finite ultrametrics encode hierarchical clustering with a fixed set of distance thresholds. It is mathematically nontrivial whether an anonymous local vertex-aggregation procedure distinguishes their complete nesting, and how many rounds it needs. The structural ball-decoding theorem gives a uniform classification guarantee, while the first one-round failure at n=8 isolates exactly how global aggregation forgets the grouping of repeated four-point clusters. The sharp minimal counterexample and complete first layer are natural benchmarks for finite-model and distance-aware graph algorithms.
